articles.title: "Why water it down?" - Sam Smith says Michael Jordan's statue makes Phil Jackson's unnecessary
articles.summary: Michael Jordan is currently the only Bulls legend the team has honored with a statue at United Center.
articles.body:
Sports teams throughout history have found various ways to honor personalities who have elevated their standing. Among the most common practices of recognizing standout athletes is unveiling statues in their honor.

NBA cities have many statues dedicated to key figures, usually located outside official team arenas. These statues not only celebrate what these luminaries have achieved but have also become prominent landmarks in the places where they stand.

One of the most notable of these NBA statues is of Chicago Bulls legend Michael Jordan . Titled "The Spirit," the figure of His Airness was unveiled on November 1, 1994, outside the United Center on the same day the Bulls retired Jordan's iconic No. 23 jersey.

The statue, which has since been moved to the arena's atrium, features the NBA great soaring through the air for a dunk, with his legs spread and the ball extended in his right hand.

"The Spirit" is the only one so far of a Bulls personality found at the United Center, although there have been conversations over the years of adding to it, particularly for that of champion coach Phil Jackson .

The Zen Master was part of the Bulls for 12 seasons. He started out as an assistant before becoming the head coach, guiding the team to six NBA titles in the 1990s, which came in two three-peats. For what he has achieved during his time in Chicago, observers believe Jackson deserves to be immortalized by the Bulls with a statue.

For longtime Bulls columnist Sam Smith , while he agrees that Jackson deserves a statue at Chi-Town, he understands why they are not in a hurry, if at all, to honor the legendary coach with his own statue.

Smith made his thoughts known in an interview with NBA Radio's David Shepard, emphasizing that having Jordan's statue already encapsulates what the Bulls represent and adding to it would hardly change that.

"The Bulls have made the point and I kind of like it in the sense that they got the number one guy of all time, Jordan, and they had a statue for Jordan. And why water it down? And it's not watering it down to say you have a statue for Phil Jackson. They've honored him, you know, retired his name or jersey number, whatever," Smith said .

"There's no sports statue that's such a worldwide important piece as the Jordan statue. So I kind of agree with that even though I think you know Phil is deserving and all this stuff and he's great coach, but, you know, the fact that they've made that Jordan statue unique and kept it as it is and because of who he is, I think it's appropriate to keep it at one statue," he added.

While there is no official word yet on whether the Bulls will honor Jackson with a statue, the Los Angeles Lakers have announced plans to unveil a bronze likeness of the coach at Crypto.com Arena next year.

Jackson, now 81, coached the Lakers for 11 seasons in the late 1990s to the 2000s with teams featuring Shaquille O'Neal and Kobe Bryant , and steered them to five championships, including three straight from 2000 to 2002.

The coach's Lakers statue is set to be unveiled on April 9, 2027, ahead of their home game against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

In 1999, Jackson was honored by the Bulls with a commemorative banner in their rafters, and in 2024, he was inducted into the inaugural class of their Ring of Honor.

Moreover, players Phil coached and fans in the Windy City appreciated how he battled and brought out the best in the Bulls teams he led, making him a true Chicago legend, with or without a statue.

articles.title: How did Valkyries' Natalie Nakase outduel Aces' Becky Hammon for Game 1 win? These 3 tactics
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO — The Golden State Valkyries entered the WNBA semifinals winless against the Las Vegas Aces in 2026. But the Aces were insistent pregame that t...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The Golden State Valkyries entered the WNBA semifinals winless against the Las Vegas Aces in 2026. But the Aces were insistent pregame that the prior record was of little significance. The teams hadn't met since June, and Aces guard Chelsea Gray said pregame that Golden State was a completely different outfit.

Las Vegas coach Becky Hammon doubled down on that idea. "The first mistake is believing that beating them 3-0 in the regular season matters," Hammon said. "It doesn't matter."

The Aces lost, and in defeat, they were proven correct. The Valkyries hardly resembled the team that had lost three times to Las Vegas during the regular season, switching up a losing game plan to take early control of the semifinals.

Although this is Golden State coach Natalie Nakase's first time leading a team in the semifinals, she spent three seasons on the bench in Las Vegas and reached at least the semis in each. That gave her an understanding of how to ready herself for the moment, and how her former mentor Hammon would prepare.

"High alert in terms of attention to detail," Nakase said when asked about what changes in the postseason. "When you have the same team over and over, you have to keep teams off rhythm."

A few tweaks to their base schemes helped Nakase and the Valkyries keep the Aces flustered.

Golden State was successful on the offensive glass throughout the season but modified its crashing principles Sunday, making a special effort for all five positions to hit the glass. Kiah Stokes had three offensive rebounds in the first three meetings against the Aces and more than doubled that total with seven. In the earlier matchups, she was only going for second efforts when she was directly underneath the basket; in the semifinals, Stokes chased offensive rebounds from the corners, making the Las Vegas bigs pay for leaving her open from 3-point range. When she was in the paint, she started boxing out early on Vegas guards' drives before the shot even went up.

Another adjustment the Valkyries made was not playing small. Golden State's second unit usually features Janelle Salaün as the center, giving the Valkyries an opportunity to spread the floor because of Salaün's long-range shooting.

The Aces, however, aren't easily beaten by the small lineups. Their guards are accustomed to defending up a position — Gray seemingly prefers to guard fours more than ones at this point of her career — and they regularly switch defensively, limiting the number 3s the opponent can get up.

Golden State decided to deliberately sacrifice its 3-point volume, staying with one true big on the court for the full 40 minutes. Instead of all five players spreading the floor, the Valkyries attacked the basket with their center. That allowed them to pick at Las Vegas' screen-and-roll defense. The Aces got lost on the back line on a couple of occasions, leading to easy finishes at the rim.

Nakase was also able to spring a surprise on her former boss. The backup center other than Salaün for most of the season has been Laeticia Amihere. For all of Amihere's athletic gifts and motor on the boards, she's a little undersized to deal with A'ja Wilson and at a strength disadvantage.

So Nakase went with the unexpected choice of Aminata Gueye, a French national who signed with Golden State for the remainder of the season on Sept. 20. The only tape Las Vegas had on Gueye with the Valkyries was four minutes of not much but missed layups in the regular-season finale and 10 minutes of garbage time in Game 1 of the first round. Even with the national team, she played only a handful of minutes at the World Cup.

But in her first meaningful action in violet, Gueye was more than the Aces bargained for. When Jackie Young attacked her in the paint, Gueye swatted the attempt away. When Gray tried to skip the ball to the right corner, Gueye was there for the interception. After a flub on a catch in the paint, Gueye recovered to finish a perfect pick-and-roll feed from her French teammate Gabby Williams and even converted the and-one.

"There's a connectivity between Gabby and Ami. … She picks up our stuff really quickly, and she's in there, obviously, to be a physical presence," Nakase said.

Hammon didn't have many counters Sunday beyond funneling even more of the offense through Wilson — never a bad idea, if defenses will allow it — and going to zone late when Las Vegas ran out of bodies. She'll have to be more creative for Game 2.

The victor of Game 1 in a best-of-five series goes on to win the series about 78 percent of the time. Hammon and the Aces have been part of that 22 percent multiple times in their three title seasons, including once against a Gabby Williams-led Storm team. Whatever tricks Nakase learned in Las Vegas, Hammon is still the reigning mastermind. She loves a puzzle, and each playoff series presents a new one.

Nakase struck first in this battle, but expect a swift comeback from Hammon. These are two of the best tacticians in the game. Even if Nakase has more pieces to play with, Hammon still has the ace in the hole.

articles.title: NBA 2K25 Is Getting Delisted After Just 2 Years, and Single Player Story Mode Will Become Unplayable
articles.summary: NBA 2K25 is being delisted after just two years, and players will soon no longer be able to play the game's single player story mode.
articles.body:
NBA 2K25 is being delisted after just two years, and players will soon no longer be able to play the game's single player story mode.

Launched back in September 2024, NBA 2K25 is the latest NBA game that is being pulled from digital stores. 2K will be pulling the game from purchase starting on October 30, 2026. Additionally, online servers will be shut down on January 1, 2027. As a result, the game's multiplayer modes and MyCareer, the game's single-player story mode, will become unplayable. MyCareer is linked to the game's online capabilities, as progression and the game's virtual currency are all dependent on a connection to the servers. If there are no servers, the mode becomes unplayable.

Those who purchase NBA 2K25 before October 30 will be able to freely download the game and play offline modes whenever they want. You can read 2K's statement on the matter below.

"As of January 1, 2027, you'll no longer be able to play multiplayer games or access any online game modes. MyCAREER and MyTEAM will no longer be available, and it will no longer be possible to earn Virtual Currency (VC). While you will still be able to enjoy Play Now, MyNBA, The W, and MyWNBA, any features that require a connection to 2K servers will be unavailable. This includes multiplayer, Online Leagues, and community sharing."

Although it's not uncommon for much older games to have their servers shut down, 2K has been delisting and killing recent NBA games in the last few years. While there's likely a very small percentage of players playing these titles anyway since the player base often moves to the current game, it is a disappointing move. It forces players to move to the new games, regardless if they want to or not. Although most sports games have modest iterations with each new entry, some titles remove features and modes, meaning some legacy content is outright non-existent anymore.

If you were a fan of NBA 2K's standalone All-Star Team-Up mode, that is no longer accessible because previous versions of the game were delisted and taken offline. It also means a lot of your effort in MyCareer is rendered somewhat useless since it has an expiration date. However, given fans keep buying the series, it doesn't seem to be hurting the franchise.

articles.title: Una estrella de la Euroliga, multada tras dar positivo en un control de alcoholemia
articles.standfirst: Carsen Edwards, escolta del Zalgiris, fue detenido durante un control rutinario por conducir en estado de embriaguez
articles.summary: Carsen Edwards, escolta del Zalgiris, fue detenido durante un control rutinario por conducir en estado de embriaguez
articles.body: El Zalgiris Kaunas multó este lunes a su jugador Carsen Edwards después de que fuese detenido en Lituania por conducir su vehículo en estado de embriaguez, según informó el propio club. Pese a que no ha dado más detallas sobre la sanción ni el positivo del escolta estadounidense, el portal lituano Krepsinis.net indicó que la tasa de alcoholemia de Edwards fue de 1,07%. El incidente se produjo durante un control policial rutinario en la noche del domingo, tan solo unas horas después de que el Zalgiris venciese al Lietkabelis en su encuentro de la liga lituana. "El Kaunas Zalgiris ha evaluado la situación del jugador Carsen Edwards, quien fue detenido al volante de un vehículo en estado de embriaguez. El club ha investigado las circunstancias del incidente y, de acuerdo con el reglamento del equipo, ha decidido imponerle una multa", dijo el club en su web. El club señaló que Edwards reconoció su error, asumió la responsabilidad de sus actos y mostró su "sincero arrepentimiento tras lo ocurrido". "El jugador comprende la gravedad de la falta cometida, reconoce que su comportamiento no estuvo a la altura de los valores del club ni de los estándares profesionales que se esperan de él, y lo lamenta profundamente", indicó. El escolta llegó este verano al Zalgiris después de su gran temporada en el Virtus Bolonia italiano. Reconocido por su capacidad para anotar, Edwards promedia esta campaña 16 puntos, 2 asistencias, un rebote y 10,3 de valoración por partido en la Euroliga. El conjunto lituano será el próximo rival del Barça en la máxima competición europea, este viernes en el Palau Blaugrana de Barcelona.

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns on chances of signing extension with Knicks before season: 'It don't look good'
articles.summary: The All-Star big man continues to sound pessimistic about his odds of signing a new deal before the start of the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
As the New York Knicks prepare to begin their NBA title defense with a preseason opener against the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday night, star big man Karl-Anthony Towns reiterated his frustration over stalled negotiations on a contract extension to remain with the Knicks for years to come.

"Simply put, I want to do something to keep the team together and can work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said Monday before the preseason opener. "And none of those things are close to happening." Asked about the possibility of an agreement before the regular season starts, Towns said, "It don't look good."

"Simply put, I want to do something to keep the team together and can work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said Monday before the preseason opener. "And none of those things are close to happening."

Asked about the possibility of an agreement before the regular season starts, Towns said, "It don't look good."

Towns, who played perhaps the best basketball of his life during New York's run to a title back in June, has one fully guaranteed season left on his contract, and holds a $61 million player option for the 2027-28 campaign. He is eligible for an extension worth a maximum of $276 million over four years — a deal with an average annual value of $69 million per season, which would make him one of the highest-paid players in the league .

The Knicks have thus far balked at that price tag, according to multiple reports . Their reluctance owes partly to the prospective perils of paying a 7-footer north of $70 million as he enters his mid-30s, but primarily to the painful financial crunch of paying to keep together a championship roster — a difficult fiscal reality that makes Towns' extension negotiation one of the most interesting to monitor in the league heading into the 2026-27 season.

As it stands, New York has just under $226.7 million in salary committed on the books for the 2027-28 season, according to Spotrac — about $9.3 million below the projected second apron line for that season. That figure includes team options on Josh Hart (who is also currently eligible for, and very much interested in, a contract extension ) and 2024 draftees Pacôme Dadiet and Tyler Kolek; it does not include a new deal for sixth man Miles "Deuce" McBride, who has dramatically outperformed his three-year, $13 million contract and is also eligible for, and very much interested in, a contract extension .

The second apron line is critical because, a scant four days after the Knicks finished off their five-game victory over the San Antonio Spurs , owner James L. Dolan went on New York radio station WFAN and made it clear that he did not intend to approve an offseason spending plan that would increase the team's total salary commitments for this season past that second apron threshold.

Dolan called the prospect of spending into the second apron something "that you'd have to be, you know, suicidal to do." Crossing that line not only imposes a higher tax rate on high-spending teams, but also strips away team-building and roster-management tools like access to salary-cap exceptions, the ability to aggregate players' salaries in trades, the option of sending cash to another team to grease the skids on a swap, and the freedom to acquire players in sign-and-trade deals, among other restrictions.

Dolan's radio-appearance edict reportedly "blindsided" the Knicks front office, which wanted to go over the second apron after patiently and meticulously building a championship roster . Instead, New York spent its summer maneuvering to stay below that $222 million line — and, in the process, lost backup center Mitchell Robinson , who signed a three-year, $47.4 million deal with the Boston Celtics .

It's unclear whether Dolan's "stay below the second apron" mandate will apply beyond this season. If it does, though, it becomes exceedingly difficult to envision a scenario in which the Knicks — who will also see Jalen Brunson and OG Anunoby become extension-eligible next summer — keep the core that just won the championship together. The math essentially demands significant financial sacrifice, beyond even the cost savings that New York was able to realize when Brunson opted to extend a year ahead of free agency and when Anunoby and Mikal Bridges took slightly less than their maximum salaries in their respective re-ups.

Towns has publicly and privately expressed a willingness to make that sort of sacrifice. The issue, of course, is just how big a sacrifice a six-time All-Star and three-time All-NBA selection who just performed at his best on the biggest stage imaginable should be expected to make.

The Knicks have reportedly offered Towns a four-year, $200 million extension — less than he got from the Timberwolves in 2022 , and more than $75 million below his max. Towns, very clearly, does not feel that offer accurately reflects the contributions he's made since arriving before the start of the 2024-25 season — a span in which he's averaged 22.2 points, 12.3 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game on 51/40/84 shooting splits, made a pair of All-Star teams and one All-NBA team, helped the Knicks reach the conference finals for the first time in a quarter-century, and then helped them hoist the Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy for the first time in 53 years.

Asked on Monday whether he felt he deserved to be rewarded for that level of achievement on his next deal, Towns told reporters : "No s***, Sherlock. I just won a championship. You'd think it was pretty easy. Unless you guys think I have something else to prove."

Towns evidently believes he's proven more than enough to merit an offer significantly above the ones New York have presented thus far — offers aimed at affording Knicks team president Leon Rose and his front office enough flexibility to try to get Brunson, Anunoby and Hart (and potentially McBride, though the math appears very tight ) extended, all while remaining under the second apron in 2028-29 and potentially beyond.

As displeased as Towns might be by the state of his negotiations, he's still under contract and set to make $57.1 million this season. The Knicks still have the opportunity to extend him at any point during the regular season — though, as Fred Katz of The Athletic recently noted , doing it before the year would allow them to extend Towns off his 2027-28 player option, unlocking potentially advantageous structures as they prepare for a major leap in Brunson's salary on his next deal.

It's also worth noting that the Knicks don't have to stay below the second apron; the league's rules don't dictate that they must, or anything. They are, as SNY's Ian Begley put it , "voluntarily limited" by Dolan's public and apparently ongoing insistence that he will not authorize spending above that line. If the owner changes his tune on that, then the tenor of Towns' negotiation — and Hart's, and McBride's, and so on — would likely change, too.

It doesn't seem like such a change is forthcoming, though. That has Towns (and Hart, and McBride, and so on) pessimistic about the prospect of getting a deal done before the start of the season, and preparing to head into a new campaign with an unwelcome uncertainty hanging over his head.

"In my experience," Towns said, according to James L. Edwards III of The Athletic , "you just approach the moments right now, and let it go where it goes."

articles.title: Vinegar, chilli powder, shattered knees: Bengaluru techie’s chilling AI queries before triple murder
articles.summary: Bengaluru triple murder probe reveals techie Kenneth allegedly used AI searches to rehearse knife attack scenarios before killing partner’s parents and sister.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Investigation into the June triple murder at Seegehalli, KR Pura, has culminated in a chilling revelation: before allegedly turning violent against his live-in partner’s family, 25-year-old techie J Kenneth allegedly used artificial intelligence (AI) to explore possible ways of attacking people.His queries included methods involving a kitchen knife, delivering fatal blows, blinding victims with vinegar and chilli powder, and incapacitating them by attacking their knees.Cops stumbled upon these details in the search history on Kenneth’s laptop, which had a disturbing pattern of AI-related searches. The questions, cops said, appeared to explore different attack scenarios and how people could be overpowered.Among the questions that surfaced in the search history were: how to fatally attack people with a kitchen knife; how to blind people using vinegar, chilli powder and chilli paste; how to shatter the knees of three people; and how to knock down three thieves who had entered a house in an isolated location.Kenneth also asked AI about the history of some of the deadliest weapons used to kill people. In another line of questioning, he sought advice on dealing with repeated calls from banks over a friend’s loan and asked how bankruptcy could be declared.For police, the sequence of questions has assumed significance because they came before Kenneth allegedly attacked his live-in partner Shwetha’s parents and sister inside their apartment on June 22.“He never asked AI what the punishment for murder would be or whether it was right to kill people who were questioning his financial inability,” a senior police officer said. “He regularly chatted with AI and treated it like a friend. He may have been academically good, but his practical knowledge and social behaviour appeared extremely poor.”Police, however, are yet to establish what answers AI provided to Kenneth. The questions were noted from the dropdown window that appeared on Google while the forensic science laboratory examined the laptop and other material.The investigation has also thrown up a striking physical detail from the crime scene: a bottle containing vinegar mixed with chilli powder. “We’ve sent it to the FSL for examination,” DCP (Whitefield division) Saidulu Adavat said.Money, rows and fatal assaultThe motive of the crime, according to the 2,085-page chargesheet filed before the city court, was rooted in money and mounting pressure on Shwetha.Shwetha, also a techie, had raised loans totalling Rs 52 lakh for Kenneth within a year. This included a Rs 30-lakh business loan, personal loans of Rs 8 lakh and Rs 6 lakh from two banks, and another Rs 8 lakh borrowed from friends, relatives, classmates and colleagues.With repayments not being made, officials of the bank that sanctioned the business loan sent a notice to Shwetha’s parents’ home.That was when the parents — Somasundar, 55, and Muthulakshmi, 50 — learnt that their daughter had borrowed a substantial amount of money, allegedly to support Kenneth. The discovery triggered a confrontation between Shwetha and her parents.Somasundar subsequently confronted Kenneth, questioning him about what he had done with the money and why the family was receiving notices over unpaid loans.Days later, on the night of June 22, the row ended in bloodshed inside their apartment at Sai Green Apartment complex in Seegehalli. Somasundar, Muthulakshmi, and their 20-year-old daughter Supriya were allegedly attacked.Somasundar, who suffered multiple injuries, managed to flee the apartment and reached the staircase. He told security personnel and others that Kenneth was attacking his wife and daughter inside.He was rushed to a private hospital but later died. articles.title: Big dreams: Suns hope young bigs can help team take next step
articles.summary: PHOENIX – Dillon Brooks has high hopes for Koa Peat. That is, if Peat can move past an issue common with rookies. “He’s a little shy,” Brooks said, “so I...
articles.body:
PHOENIX – Dillon Brooks has high hopes for Koa Peat . That is, if Peat can move past an issue common with rookies.

"He's a little shy," Brooks said, "so I got to break that wall."

Peat is one of at least four young bigs whom the Suns veterans hope will break down walls and earn significant playing time this season. That has been a key theme for the team as it begins the preseason on Monday in Detroit.

The Suns finished 45-37 last season, earning an eighth-place finish in the Western Conference. After advancing past the play-in round, Oklahoma City swept them. Still, it was a major improvement from the previous season when Phoenix finished 10 games below .500 and missed the playoffs.

With the help of some veterans, the Suns are hoping to build on last season's success by getting big contributions from their last two top draft picks and a crop of young bigs.

Heading into the preseason, Suns veterans have spoken highly of second-year center Khaman Maluach, who was the 10th overall pick in the 2025 NBA draft, second-year forward Rasheer Fleming and rookie forward Koa Peat, who won four state championships at Gilbert Perry High and helped Arizona to a Final Four before the Suns selected him 30th overall in the 2026 NBA draft.

The Suns obtained the draft rights to Maluach as part of the trade that sent Kevin Durant to Houston. Fleming, who was originally drafted by Minnesota, was also part of that seven-team blockbuster.

Maluach saw few minutes on the court during his rookie year, appearing in 46 games and starting only once. Fleming also started just one game and played in 55 as a rookie. But Maluach made big strides in the offseason, and the big man's prospects look different this season.

Maluach averaged 19.5 points, 12.8 rebounds and had two blocks in the 2026 NBA Summer League, leading the league in rebounds averaged and earning second-team All-NBA Summer League honors.

Then came the news that center Mark Williams, whom the Suns had just re-signed and was the likely starter, would miss an indefinite amount of time after shoulder surgery.

"I pray for Mark," Maluach said. "That's my teammate. It's an opportunity for me to step up, but I'm here to do whatever it takes, what the team needs. That's how I see it and I'm going to do whatever it takes for us to be in a good spot."

Williams' absence gives Maluach a chance to break into the rotation and possibly the starting lineup, but he'll be competing with former Phoenix Desert Vista High star Oso Ighodaro for the starting center spot. Ighodaro is entering his third year in the league.

"It puts more (pressure) on Oso and Man-Man (Maluach)," Suns coach Jordan Ott said. "These two guys are ultra-competitive, ultra-young. They understand that they have to play with a certain type of physicality. These two centers battle it every day."

Despite the competition, Ighodaro said it's all love between the players and that helps them push each other to be better.

"I love playing with him," Ighodaro said. "Even in pickup when we'll be on opposite teams, we'll be talking to each other, helping each other, giving each other pointers. I feel like we both have a similar mindset in terms of the process and getting better. I'm grateful to have him as my teammate."

During the offseason, Maluach reached out to Suns star Devin Booker and asked to work out with him to build a better connection.

"He has done this for a long time," Maluach said. "He has a lot of tools or a lot of stuff that I can learn from him. As a young center, just being able to go to him and being able to ask him what I should do. He's kind of like a coach himself and I get to learn a lot from him."

Maluach isn't the only player learning from vets. Peat, who averaged 14.1 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.6 assists during his only season at Arizona, has benefitted as well. The Suns pulled some strings during the draft to obtain him, sending the 47th pick in 2026, two future second-round picks and cash considerations to the New York Knicks for the 30th pick.

"We had Koa much higher in our rankings," Suns general manager Brian Gregory said. "As the night progressed and it looked like there might be an opportunity for us to pull a couple of levers to be in position, the excitement grew and grew. Everywhere he's been, all he's done is win."

Ighodaro isn't surprised the Suns pursued his fellow Valley local.

"He doesn't carry himself like a rookie," Ighodaro said. "He wants to learn. He wants to get better. He's an extremely good rebounder. He guards the ball defensively. If he continues to do so, he'll impact winning."

Suns guard Jalen Green said the veterans will shepherd Peat.

"He's going to learn a lot from everybody on the team," Green said. "Especially like Booker, Miles (Bridges). He's got that bump. He's playing mid-range. He's got a mid-range shot. Can't ask for nothing else, and just learning the whole summer."

Fleming is another player hoping to break into the rotation.

"He continues to raise the floor by his work, his care and his understanding of who he is as a player," Ott said of Fleming. "He has no idea where his ceiling is, nor do we. He has physical gifts that you cannot teach."

Green also took note of Fleming's work ethic.

"That's who he is as a player," Green said. "I don't see anything else but him continuing to do that. I'll see him be in the gym in the morning and come back at night. He loves the work and he's putting that time in."

Booker said the young players as a whole have displayed a work ethic and attention to detail that will serve them and the team well.

"They're always the first in the gym," Booker said. "They bring their youth and energy every day. They're getting extra shots up. They all ask the right questions. I haven't seen a bad rookie or a bad young fella in a while now."

articles.title: Kansas State ends Jerome Tang dispute with a $12M settlement after firing
articles.summary: MANHATTAN, Kansas (AP) — Kansas State has reached a settlement with former basketball coach Jerome Tang that includes a $12 million payment.The athletic depa...
articles.body:
MANHATTAN, Kansas (AP) — Kansas State has reached a settlement with former basketball coach Jerome Tang that includes a $12 million payment.

The athletic department and Tang announced the agreement Monday, ending a dispute that arose after the former Wildcats coach was fired for cause in February, threatening to void an $18.7 million buyout.

"This settlement allows both parties to move forward on agreed terms," Kansas State athletic director Gene Taylor said in a statement. "We're grateful for his contributions to Kansas State basketball, including a memorable first season, and we wish him and his family well."

Kansas State announced it was firing Tang on Feb. 15, four days after a 29-point loss to Cincinnati.

After the game, a despondent Tang said that his players "do not deserve to wear this uniform" and that "there will be very few of them in it next year." The sound bite quickly made headlines, and the school ultimately fired Tang for cause, saying that he had embarrassed the school.

Tang told ESPN at the time that he disagreed with the "characterization of my termination." He also disputed the "for cause" nature of his dismissal.

In four seasons at Kansas State, the 59-year-old Tang was 71-57 overall and 29-39 in the Big 12. He led the Wildcats to a 26-10 mark and the Elite Eight, becoming the first head coach in program history to receive the Naismith Men's Basketball Coach of the Year Award.

In June, Tang rejoined Baylor coach Scott Drew's staff as associate head coach. Tang was on Drew's staff the first 19 seasons before going to Kansas State.

articles.title: Knicks' Mike Brown Praises 'Loaded' 76ers After LeBron, Brown Additions, Admits East 'Got Harder'
articles.summary: Mike Brown led the New York Knicks to a title in his first season as head coach, but he knows it's going to be much harder to repeat this year.
articles.body:
Mike Brown led the New York Knicks to a title in his first season as head coach, but he knows it's going to be much harder to repeat this year.

Brown praised the "loaded" Philadelphia 76ers after they added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, and admitted that making it out of the Eastern Conference is going to be "harder."

"In my opinion, it definitely just got harder for everybody with the team that they assembled," Brown told reporters on Monday.

The 76ers already had a talented team with Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey leading the way, but they added an all-time great in James and a former Finals MVP in Brown, who is coming off the best season of his career.

But the talent in the East isn't limited to just the Sixers.

The Miami Heat also upgraded their roster this offseason, pairing Giannis Antetokounmpo alongside Bam Adebayo. Miami also added one of the best shooters in NBA history in Klay Thompson.

Getting through the East was relatively easy for the Knicks last year, but it's going to be a much different story this year.

articles.title: LeBron James’ wife Savannah James’ latest flight incident offers an important rich-people financial lesson as the internet argues over dopamine-hitting morality
articles.summary: It’s not easy to be rich.
articles.body: It’s not easy to be rich. While LeBron James has built his massive financial empire from his career earnings, several business ventures, and endorsements, his wife, Savannah James, is slowly climbing the ladder to create her own financial empire. Recently, news of Savannah and her best friend, April McDaniel, broke online. Fans were quite upset, most of them anyway, and the reason for their big upset was that dopamine-hitting morality was missing from the picture. The two laid out the arrangement on the Sept. 28 episode of Boardroom's Mental Wealth podcast, and the clip has been fought over online ever since.But that was the point, McDaniel was not upset, and her account secretly revealed an important lesson. Let’s have a look at what happened first and how their reactions to the incident gave away a subtle message about money.Savannah James and April McDaniel on their flight arrangementThe hosts, Rich Kleiman and Jack Howard, opened with a broad question about how friendship and money mix, and the exchange came about four minutes into the episode. McDaniel answered first. She said the two live different lifestyles and neither pretends otherwise.It shows in how they travel. McDaniel can't take a spontaneous trip, so the pair book well ahead, which keeps costs down, and James leaves enough time for McDaniel to get her finances lined up. They don't turn up at Fashion Week on a week's notice, whatever people assume about how they move. On a recent trip, reportedly to Japan according to local media, James took first class and McDaniel took business. First was outside what McDaniel planned to spend, and she saw no reason to match James seat for seat. They laugh about it, she said.The two are not casual travel companions. They have been friends for well over a decade, and McDaniel described the move into business together as organic. They co-host the podcast Everybody's Crazy and run a holding company called Signed, and James owns the skincare brand, Reframe Beauty. McDaniel also runs a creative agency.The seat split had come up on their own show before the Mental Wealth appearance, McDaniel said, and some viewers were openly critical. One detail seemed to bother people most. During flights, she goes up front, gets into James' bed and watches a movie with her. “And I was like: ‘Why? I can't afford first,'” April said.The hosts then asked James whether friends had ever expected her to cover a first-class seat for them.Critics and defenders split over the seat gapCelebrity Net Worth puts Savannah's wealth near $100 million.Critics started with cost. A $10,000 fare is very negligible for Savannah. Others said withholding an upgrade felt like a quiet reminder that the two women are not on the same level. A few wanted James to either buy the ticket or sit in economy with her friend. Some asked why anyone would sit alone on a long flight just to prove a point.Paying with points does not make the seat free, since taxes and fees still have to be paid in cash and can run into the thousands.Commenters argued that paying once invites more, first the spa day and then the dinner check. Boundaries, in this view, are what let a friendship survive a wealth gap, and handouts can breed resentment or entitlement. Praise went to McDaniel for staying within her means and to James for not letting friends become moochers.Former Knicks star Brandon Jennings sided with them on X. His post, from @Tuff__Crowd: "If you can't afford first class or certain things when you around your rich friends and you feel entitled that they should pay, Ur a certified moocher…Savannah James ain't wrong."Savannah and McDaniel respond to the backlashMcDaniel called it ridiculous to assume everybody should fly first and said expectations need managing. She described a recent run-in with someone stunned that she flies commercial instead of private, and she played it for laughs by asking the person if they were okay. In her view, social media has bent people's sense of what things cost, and people used to fast money treat it differently than people who earn it slowly. She wants others to know it is fine to live a normal life.Her rule for money is to worry about yourself. The two live in separate worlds, she said, and meet up to talk about them. She credits James with adjusting to where she is financially, and says the friendship runs on feel. If a plan doesn't feel good to both of them, they skip it.James spoke to the other half of the question. Her friends, she said, understand the situation before any trip begins, and every one of them respects it. Nobody has asked her to take care of a cost or be responsible for them. It "has never, ever been that," she said. She voiced gratitude for that understanding.McDaniel stressed that the friendship holds because each side respects the other's finances.The money lesson inside the seat splitOn the podcast, two women with very different bank balances said out loud what each can spend, and neither apologized for her number. They didn’t have to.Howard, who leads money wellness at Ally and has taught budgeting for 16 years, shared that she believes a bank account should show a person's values, and for most people it doesn't. She opens with a question about a person's first memory of money, because she sees two common mistakes, people don't know their money story, and they don't know what they value now. Neither is a math problem. Shame does more damage than arithmetic. Someone who can't afford brunch puts it on a card instead of saying so. Her fix is one honest sentence that offers a cheaper plan, because once it is said, "shame loses its power."James described her own version. Her tax bracket and the prices around her have changed, she said, but her view of what things are worth has not. Spending that follows values makes the seat choice easy for both women: McDaniel pays for what fits her plan, and James pays for what fits hers.Of course, the higher earner does not have to match a friend's standard of living, and saying what each person can afford keeps the relationship steady. Experts also advise telling friends honestly how much you can spend before signing up for travel or dinners.Howard offers a practical start for anyone with uneven income. Fold a sheet of paper into three columns and log every expense, the emotion behind it and the value it served. articles.body: Dillon Brooks and John Collins needed less than five minutes of Monday night's preseason opener between the Suns and Pistons to put hands on each other. A hard foul on an offensive rebound set it off, and players from both teams stepped in to pull them apart.The penalties were small, but the clip spread quickly, and the reaction split between laughter and disbelief. Lead official Karl Lane said Collins' actions were unnecessary. Phoenix shot two free throws, Detroit shot one, and play went on. ESPN's NBA account posted the clip with a note on the early intensity. It was the first exhibition game of the year for both clubs, played Oct. 5.There were no dirty plays, only small shots that piled up until both men went for the rebound. Many would agree that the throat grab was an overreaction for a preseason game.NBA fans react to Brooks and Collins scuffleThe clip went viral on the internet, and fans jumped into the comment sections of social media sites for their takes on the matter. articles.body: LeBron James (41 años) no jugó en el primer partido de temporada de los Philadelphia 76ers, con los que sí debutó Jaylen Brown en el triunfo de los Sixers 120-97 ante los New York Knicks, vigentes campeones de la NBA. Jaylen Brown brilló con 22 puntos (8 de 13 en tiros de campo) en sólo 16 minutos. VJ Edgecombe (12 puntos), Jabari Walker (11 puntos y 11 rebotes), Caleb Love (15 puntos), Dillon Jones (11 puntos) y Saint Thomas (11 puntos y 10 rebotes) fueron los otros jugadores de los Sixers, con los que tampoco jugó Joel Embiid, con dobles dígitos. articles.title: John Collins Grabs Dillon Brooks by Throat, Reacts to Fight After Pistons vs. Suns Preseason Game
articles.summary: It didn't take Dillon Brooks long to get into his first scuffle of the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
It didn't take Dillon Brooks long to get into his first scuffle of the 2026-27 season.

Within the first five minutes of Monday's preseason game against the Detroit Pistons, the Phoenix Suns guard incited an incident by repeatedly fouling John Collins on a rebound. Collins responded by turning around and grabbing Brooks' throat, which led to the scuffle:

Collins addressed it after the game and told reporters he "wasn't necessarily trying to set that tone, but I'm glad I did. Just sometimes you have to play basketball and get physical. I'm going to go out there and compete every night."

Detroit signed Collins to a three-year deal this offseason, so this was quite the introduction to the home fans.

Of course, he is far from the first player to have a similar interaction with Brooks. The Suns guard has "Dillon the Villain" listed as his nickname on Basketball Reference for a reason and has never hesitated to get physical or trash talk opponents.

He also led the league with 17 technical fouls last season.

If Monday's game was any indication, Brooks will probably pick up a few technical fouls in 2026-27 as well.

articles.title: Philadelphia 76ers injury update: LeBron James’ teammate suffers serious injury prompting early exit against Knicks
articles.summary: Ariel Hukporti started at center for the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday. However, he had to leave the game before even hitting the six-minute mark.
articles.body: Ariel Hukporti started at center for the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday. However, he had to leave the game before even hitting the six-minute mark. Hukporti dropped to the floor on a non-contact play against his old team, the New York Knicks, and had to be helped off. Philadelphia still won the preseason opener 120-97 at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Joel Embiid, LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey sat the game out, so the starting five was patchwork from the jump. The Sixers were already short on centers before tipoff, and Tuesday's imaging may show how thin they are.What happened to Ariel Hukporti against the Knicks?New York had its full title-winning starting group on the floor. With 7:06 left in the first quarter, Hukporti took an awkward step back while guarding Karl-Anthony Towns. He went down right away and grabbed the lower right leg. Nobody had touched him. He was helped off during the next timeout and did not come back.The $3.4 million center signed a one-year deal with Philadelphia in July after winning a title with the Knicks. Hukporti had impressed in the Blue and White scrimmage over the weekend, so the Knicks game looked like a chance to build on it.Coach Nick Nurse said after the game that Hukporti will get imaging on the right Achilles on Tuesday.Philadelphia pulled away anyway behind Jaylen Brown, who scored 13 of his 22 points in the first quarter.The current Sixers roster situationHukporti and Adem Bona came into camp competing for the top backup job behind Embiid, so one is out and the other has not started. Bona has not taken part in camp after spraining his left foot while playing for Turkey's national team. Tacko Fall, the 7-foot-5 camp invitee, has a left hip sprain and will be reevaluated in about two weeks. Dominick Barlow is dealing with a setback of his own. Embiid is healthy in camp but has missed 150 games over the past three seasons.Jabari Walker gave the Sixers 11 points and 11 rebounds in 24 minutes against the Knicks. His contract is not fully guaranteed until Jan. 10.The Athletic's Tony Jones reports the Sixers like the setup they have now, even without Hukporti. Philadelphia has an open roster spot, but it is expected to stay empty for the first few months of the season, and any emergency signing would need follow-up moves to work financially.Philadelphia visits Brooklyn on Thursday and Boston on Saturday before hosting Boston on Oct. 16. Nurse hopes to have most of the roster healthy for two of those three games. articles.summary: It's just preseason, but the post-LeBron James era is off to a solid start for the Los Angeles Lakers.
articles.body:
It's just preseason, but the post-LeBron James era is off to a solid start for the Los Angeles Lakers.

Los Angeles cruised against the Sacramento Kings in Monday's preseason contest with future Hall of Famer Luka Dončić leading the way and Bronny James receiving solid playing time. There was plenty of time to go around, as Walker Kessler (finger) and Austin Reaves (ankle) were both out with injuries.

Dončić was brilliant as usual and looked ready for another All-Star campaign, while James played a role off the bench.

Los Angeles wasted no time setting the tone with a 73-47 halftime advantage thanks in large part to Dončić's contributions. He poured in 21 points before intermission as he connected from beyond the arc, attacked the lane, got to the free-throw line and created opportunities in transition.

He also facilitated when defenders collapsed on him, which made life easier for all his teammates. Quentin Grimes found his scoring stroke early, while Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Jake LaRavia all drained multiple threes.

It was clear the offense is going to run through Dončić with LeBron James no longer on the roster, and he already looked to be in midseason form.

In fact, he was so effective there was no need for the Lakers to play him in the second half.

Bronny James, on the other hand, saw the court in the second half. The third-year playmaker has never been more than a secondary playmaker off the bench for Los Angeles, so it came as no surprise head coach JJ Redick gave him an opportunity to make an impact in the preseason.

While the USC product certainly didn't take over as a scorer, he impacted the game in other ways by crashing the boards and dishing out multiple assists. He also hit from three-point range.

That three-point shooting will be important if he is going to earn playing time this season, as the defensive attention Dončić draws should create a number of open looks.

He will have another chance to make a preseason impact Thursday when the Lakers face the Golden State Warriors.

articles.title: El mito de Bolong Zheng: el base chino que 'paga' por jugar y que le metió un triple al Madrid en ACB

articles.summary: Bolong Zheng lleva una década haciendo carrera en el baloncesto profesional de España logrando huecos en plantillas gracias a acuerdos comerciales
articles.body: El Bueno Arenas Albacete Basket, equipo que milita en Primera FEB, ha anunciado el fichaje del jugador chino Bolong Zheng (36 años). "El club incorpora a Bolong Zheng dentro de un acuerdo de colaboración alcanzado con una firma deportiva y empresarial china", informó el equipo que entrena David Varela. Radio MARCA Albacete informa que "la llegada Bolong Zheng al equipo albaceteño se enmarca, principalmente, dentro de un acuerdo de colaboración comercial, patrocinio e internacionalización, que permitirá al club reforzar sus vínculos con el mercado chino y abrir nuevas vías de crecimiento y generación de recursos para el proyecto". Bolong Zheng (1989) es un jugador chino formado en la Universidad de Kansas State que lleva una década haciendo carrera en el baloncesto profesional de España logrando huecos en plantillas gracias a acuerdos comerciales. A lo largo de su carrera el base de 1,83 m. de Shaanxi ha jugado para Movistar Estudiantes (Tercer FEB), Fuenlabrada (Liga Endesa), Ourense (Primera FEB), Lucentum Alicante (Primera FEB) y Montemar (Tercer FEB). La primera parada en España de Bolong Zheng fue el Amics Castelló, desde donde se marchó al CB Vinaròs. En 2017 Zheng volvió a España para firmar por Movistar Estudiantes, gracias al acuerdo de colaboración que el conjunto madrileño tenía con Guangzhou Longlions. El jugador chino permaneció dos temporadas trabajando con el equipo EBA, aunque no llegó a debutar con el primer equipo colegial. Durante su paso en el HLA Alicante en 2024, la alianza con el grupo empresarial chino Guanou Sports incluyó una estancia de pretemporada y una gira de 10 días para todo el equipo en China. Bolong Zheng hizo historia en marzo de 2022 al convertirse en el primer baloncestista chino en debutar y anotar en la Liga ACB (Liga Endesa) mientras jugaba con el Baloncesto Fuenlabrada en un partido contra el Real Madrid, en el que anotó un triple. "El momento del debut fue fascinante para mí. Disfruté cada momento en la pista. Es un sueño hecho realidad, con todo el trabajo anterior... es un momento inolvidable para el resto de mi vida, sin duda. Ya desde que llegamos al pabellón y en el calentamiento estaba emocionado a la vez que centrado en el partido y esperando la posibilidad de que el entrenador me llamara para jugar. Estoy contento de haber anotado el triple que lancé", contó Zheng a MARCA en 2022.

articles.title: Doncic toma el poder en los Lakers post LeBron y rediseña su identidad en 16 minutos mágicos
articles.standfirst: Los Lakers mostraron pinceladas de su nueva identidad defensiva en la victoria ante los Sacramento Kings
articles.summary: Los Lakers mostraron pinceladas de su nueva identidad defensiva en la victoria ante los Sacramento Kings
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers ganaron 103-127 a los Sacramento Kings en el primer partido de la era post LeBron James, que no jugó con los Sixers en su estreno en la pretemporada NBA. Luka Doncic, el indiscutible líder de los Lakers tras la salida de 'King' James, fue el mejor de los de púrpura y oro en el Golden 1 Center de Sacramento con 21 puntos, 3 rebotes, 2 asistencias y 2 robos en apenas 16 minutos (no jugó en la segunda parte). Los Lakers, que jugaron sin los lesionados Austin Reaves y Walker Kessler, mostraron una presión a toda cancha para exhibir una identidad defensiva más agresiva e incisiva. Doncic recibió un rodillazo en el cuádriceps a mediados del segundo cuarto, pero permaneció en el partido. Dado que los Lakers ganaban por 26 puntos al descanso, Luka no volvió a jugar. Después de que los Kings incurrieran en una violación del reloj de posesión en la primera jugada del partido Doncic alzó los puños hacia el banquillo de los Lakers con una sonrisa triunfal, celebrando ese comienzo exitoso. "Creo que, por primera vez desde que estoy aquí, contamos con varios jugadores capaces de presionar al rival desde toda la pista y generar problemas en el punto de ataque. Vamos a pedirles que hagan precisamente eso", reconoció el entrenador JJ Redick antes del partido. Ziaire Williams (13 puntos), Quentin Grimes (16 puntos), Jake LaRavia (12 puntos), Cameron Carr (19 puntos) y Chris Mañon (12 puntos) fueron los otros jugadores de los Lakers que firmaron dobles dígitos. Los mejores de los Kings fueron Darius Acuff Jr. (19 puntos), Dylan Cardwell (9 puntos y 10 rebotes), Daeqwon Plowden (12 puntos), Maxime Raynaud (12 puntos) y Nique Clifford (23 puntos).

articles.title: ‘I Can’t Even Believe This,’ ‘So Eager To Break (Caitlin Clark) and (Kelsey Mitchell) Up’ — WNBA World Pushes Back As ESPN Hypes Fever Star’s Free Agency
articles.summary: On Monday, ESPN’s Ramona Shelburne and Chiney Ogwumike made the case that teams want to build around Kelsey Mitchell as a franchise player as she hits unrest...
articles.body:
On Monday, ESPN's Ramona Shelburne and Chiney Ogwumike made the case that teams want to build around Kelsey Mitchell as a franchise player as she hits unrestricted free agency.

Mitchell, who has played all nine of her seasons with the Indiana Fever, recently said during the Indiana Fever's exit interviews that she would put herself first and be "selfish" as she makes her decision.

The Las Vegas Aces ended Indiana's season for the second-straight year, winning 94-83 in Thursday's first-round Game 3 after eliminating the Fever in the 2025 semifinals.

Will Kelsey Mitchell Remain With Caitlin Clark and Fever or Leave in Free Agency?

"This is an MVP candidate," Shelburne said. "There are teams that would want to build around a franchise player like that. If she's available? Whew."

Ogwumike added that she's a "plug-and-play player" who "can play on any team because she just fits within systems and is a tremendous scorer."

Mitchell is coming off a career year in which she averaged 24.7 points per game and set WNBA single-season records for points and 3-pointers. In April, Mitchell signed a one-year, $1.4 million supermax deal to return to Indiana, but now her future is up in the air.

"I have to be selfish," Mitchell said on Saturday, explaining that she has to weigh what is best for her at this stage of her career. The Fever gave her the core designation over the past two seasons and cannot use it on her again.

Several fans replied to Shelburne and Ogwumike's analysis, arguing that Indiana already tried building around her.

"Last time a team tried to build around her, they had the #1 pick in back-to-back years. I have grown to really like KM, but she is not a #1 player on a winning team," one fan wrote.

The Fever used back-to-back No. 1 picks on Aliyah Boston in 2023 and Caitlin Clark in 2024. Mitchell, taken No. 2 behind A'ja Wilson in 2018, reached her first postseason in 2024, Indiana's first playoff trip since 2016.

"Can someone help me understand how Kelsey Mitchell wasn't good enough to carry a franchise to the playoffs from 2018-2023 but is now? What changed?" another fan wrote .

Others said Mitchell's series against Las Vegas hurt her stock entering free agency.

"She shot the Fever out of the playoffs shooting just 32% the entire series. Go for it," one critic added.

Mitchell shot 4-of-16, 7-of-16, and 7-of-23 from the field in the three games, though she led Indiana with 23 points in Game 3.

Clark said after Game 3 that the Fever had made a lot of those shots throughout the year. "So if we would have ran it back, who knows, me and Kels maybe make another combined eight shots, and it's a completely different game," Clark said.

Mitchell said Saturday that playing in a backcourt with Clark is something she values and will factor into her decision.

However, Mitchell also stated that the hate she gets in her direct messages is a lot, and added that Clark's teammates take criticism just for being on her team.

"Fever and Clark fans doing our work for us! And when I say our, I mean whatever team Kelsey Mitchell (hopefully Atlanta) she decides to go to. So please you Fever fans, keep posting Kelsey Mitchell content," another fan wrote.

Other fans were annoyed by the analysis, arguing that ESPN was trying to break up Indiana's duo of Clark and Mitchell.

"They are literally salivating at the thought of breaking up that duo. I can't even believe this," one fan added .

"They are so eager to break cc and km up 😭" another fan wrote .

"She's meant so much to us and has obviously had, arguably, the best season in the history of our league in terms of being a scoring guard," Fever general manager Amber Cox said.

Head coach Stephanie White called Mitchell's free agency the Fever's top priority, and Cox added that the goal is for Mitchell to retire in a Fever uniform.

articles.title: Darius Acuff Jr. looked comfortable in his first NBA preseason game
articles.summary: Sacramento Kings guard Darius Acuff Jr. had a solid outing in his first NBA preseason game.
articles.body:
SACRAMENTO, CA ― Darius Acuff Jr. wasn't too worried about his offense in his first ever preseason game. The Sacramento Kings rookie looked comfortable as if he's already entering his seventh NBA season.

He scored 19 points in 27 minutes in his first NBA action, albeit in just a preseason game, despite his team coming short in a 127-103 loss to the Los Angeles Lakers on Monday, Oct. 6 at Golden 1 Center in downtown Sacramento.

"It felt good. I haven't played a game in a while, like a real game," Acuff told USA TODAY Sports. "It felt good, just get out there and play against somebody else. Not the outcome we wanted but it was good to play against somebody else."

Acuff, the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft , didn't have anything to say about his offensive performance. He added four assists, a block and steal to his stat line. His main gripe came on the defensive end as the Lakers shot 50% from the field, including 45% from 3-point territory on 20 made 3-point field goals.

"I don't think offense is the problem," he said. "I think, with defensively, we just wasn't racking up stops as a team, as much as we needed to. I think that's kind of what separated the game. But I think offensively, we'll be fine."

And they will. Acuff did not seem phased by a Lakers defense that picked him up full court, 94 feet throughout the duration of the game whenever he logged minutes.

The Kings rookie said it's better practice for him. He welcomes the challenge. He wants the pressure.

"It was the same," Acuff said. "It was better for me, picking me up full court. I feel like I like to play against that, so I think that's an advantage for me.

"Yeah, for sure. It prepares me for sure," he added. "I say, it takes watching film, just being smart, and, you know, not trying to dribble the air out the ball back there, just trying to get one move and go. But (it) definitely prepares me for the better defenders I'm gonna face, and, you know, I just gotta take the challenge, and, you know, go out there and be me."

Fun NBA media day moments from teams across the league

Kings head coach Doug Christie echoed the same sentiment as his star rookie point guard that their defense has to be better.

"You know, helping when you're not supposed to help, like all the principles of shell defense, help defense, being in a gap, being in to be out, closing out, more middle," Christie told USA TODAY. "I'm sure the film's going to show all of that. But this is what we do. We learn, we go back to the film, we show them, we drill it, we get after it."

There's no panic in Christie, Acuff or the rest of the Kings. It's the first preseason game. But there is room for improvement and lots of it.

Kings forward-guard Daeqwon Plowden said preseason games are supposed to be evaluated differently.

"It's the first one outside of us playing each other, so we're setting the standard. The way we're evaluated is going to be much higher than what it was," Plowden told USA TODAY. "I think it's a lot that we can take away from this and build on."

Christie proclaimed the team will "be better."

"You know, they got hit in the mouth," he said. "And how do we respond?"

articles.title: Isa Latorre y su canasta imposible: "Salió cara, te hace estar en un nube"
articles.standfirst: La base del Movistar Estudiantes cuenta cómo fue su triple milagroso desde 20 metros que dio el triunfo al equipo colegial ante el Girona en la primera jornada de la Liga Femenina
articles.summary: La base del Movistar Estudiantes cuenta cómo fue su triple milagroso desde 20 metros que dio el triunfo al equipo colegial ante el Girona en la primera jornada de la Liga Femenina
articles.body: Como teníamos ensayado el saque rápido, que siempre nos da mucho, la verdad es que Laia sacó muy rápido y hubo conexión. Nos miramos las dos y tras la canasta de Iyana me pasó la pelota. Después de eso, pues ya lo hemos visto todo, que el tiro salió cara”. Así cuenta Isa Latorre (1996, Alcantarilla, Murcia) el triple desde su propia pista que abrió de manera estupenda la Liga Femenina Endesa 26-27, una de las primeras canastas del año en los albores de una temporada que arrancó el pasado sábado en el Magariños con emociones fuertes. El Movistar Estudiantes ganó al Spar Girona de Iyana Martín (82-79) con una acción inhabitual desde casi 20 metros que la base murciana recordará siempre por extraordinaria. Esto ni se entrena específicamente ni se trabaja. Simplemente, se intenta. La desesperación se asocia a veces con la puntería. "Es verdad que hacemos tiros desde medio de campo por la mañana, en la sesión de tiro, donde se falla y se acierta. Por la mañana fallé y me tocaba pagar algo. Espero que la canasta de por la tarde se convalide", dice, medio de broma, mientras recuerda el prodigio para MARCA 48 horas después. La base de 30 años, con una sólida carrera a sus espaldas desde sus inicios en Alcantarilla, la casa del Jairis, una trayectoria labrada en plata en el segundo escalón del baloncesto femenino, con pasado luminoso en el Leganés, con el que consiguió un ascenso histórico en 2021, y Zamora, con el que disputó la LF Challenge, forma parte de la plantilla del Estudiantes desde 2024. Con las colegiales se asentó en la élite. Ahora, una acción suya ha caído en las garras lo viral. Aunque siempre puso por delante al equipo, pese a que picó mucha piedra sin trascender en exceso para el gran público en un baloncesto puro, el de la segunda categoría del básket femenino, pero también opaco, celebra la notoriedad, sobre todo la utilidad de la asombrosa canasta: el triunfo de las llamadas ‘Woman in black’ ante uno de los ‘grandes’ de la Liga Femenina, el Girona. Bendita visibilidad. "Al principio estás como en un nube. No sabía ni dónde estaba. Vienen mis compañeras a felicitarme y después hay un momento en que me quedo diciendo 'vamoooos' a la cámara. Se me ve a mí sola. Creo que caí en la importancia de la jugada unos minutos más tarde. Al llegar al vestuario me decían, "tú estás loca". Latorre, base de 1,70, dirige al Movistar Estudiantes en la cancha con una gran lectura del juego. Su perspectiva de la vida también es amplia. Siempre reparó en las necesidades psicológicas de la jugadora de élite. Pregona la importancia del psicólogo deportivo en los staffs de los equipos. A la hora de tomar conciencia en ese sentido siempre se mostró franca sobre la necesidad del deportista de tener un asesoramiento psicológico para no acusar en exceso la presión y asimilar la derrota y los días malos. Cree que es fundamental la ayuda para la gestión del fracaso y reivindica el trato humano para el deportista porque “somos personas antes que jugadores profesionales”. Ahora debe asimilar otra cosa, cierta fama que nunca tuvo. Firmaba autógrafos en el Ramiro antes de atender a MARCA. "La verdad es que siempre suelo estar más en la sombra. Yo al final pongo siempre por delante al equipo antes que a mí como jugadora. Y bueno, tenemos la suerte que este año el equipo somos como una trainera, una embarcación de remo de la que tiran todos. Tengo los pies en la tierra. Sé quién soy. Y por suerte la gente que me rodea también está conmigo cuando fallo. Eso es lo más importante", cuenta una de las primeras candidatas al premio de la FEB y MARCA a la canasta del año. Y el espectáculo de la Liga Femenina acaba de empezar.

articles.title: La Euroliga mira al futuro: un plan estratégico para los próximos 10 años
articles.standfirst: Los accionistas estudian hoy la conversión de licencias en franquicias. Analizarán socios de expansión nuevos. Y decidirán cómo proceder en las conversaciones en curso con la NBA
articles.summary: Los accionistas estudian hoy la conversión de licencias en franquicias. Analizarán socios de expansión nuevos. Y decidirán cómo proceder en las conversaciones con la NBA
articles.body: La lujosa Villa d'Este, situada a orillas del Lago de Como, acoge hoy la Asamblea General de la Euroliga más importante en sus 26 años de historia pues en ella se decidirá el futuro de la competición. No es casual la elección de ese emblemático enclave, que durante décadas ha acogido importantes reuniones internacionales. Un lugar donde se han sentado a puerta cerrada dirigentes políticos, económicos y empresariales de todo el mundo para abordar cambios de gran calado. La Asamblea de la Euroliga será lo más parecido a una reunión de jefes de Estado, trasladada al baloncesto europeo. No hay más que mirar la nómina de asistentes para darse cuenta de la trascendencia de la misma, pues están presentes los máximos ejecutivos de los 13 clubes accionistas que son los propietarios de la competición, e incluso algunos de sus dueños, dada la trascendencia de esta cumbre de máximo nivel. Sobre ellos recae la responsabilidad de la toma de decisiones que marcará el futuro de la competición y de decenas de los clubes más punteros del Viejo Continente. El primer punto del orden del día será aprobar un plan estratégico para los próximos 10 años; el segundo, estudiar la conversión de licencias en franquicias; el tercero, analizar las propuestas de al menos 13 equipos que han presentado ofertas garantizadas y aspiran a ser nuevos socios en el proyecto de expansión de franquicias; y cuarto y último punto del orden del día, pero no por ello menos importante, el decidir cómo proceder en las conversaciones que ya están en curso con la NBA. Vista la trascendencia de la reunión no es extraño que hayan acudido 36 de los máximos ejecutivos de los 13 clubes propietarios. Destacan el presidente del Anadolu Efes, Tuncay Ozilhan, el del Armani Milan, Pantaleo Dell’Orco, el del Bayern Munich, Herbert Hainer, el del Fenerbahce, Derya Yannier, el del ASVEL Villeurbanne, Tony Parker, o el del Zalgiris, Paulius Motiejunas. Incluso son varios los propietarios de equipos que no han querido perderse la cita, como el dueño del CSKA Moscú, Andrey Batutin, el del Maccabi Tel Aviv, Simon Mizrahi, los del Olympiacos, Georgios y Panagiotis Angelopoulos, o el archienemigo de ambos, Dimitris Giannakopoulos, propietario del Panathinaikos. Los tres representantes españoles también han mandado su artillería pesada. Allí estarán Joan Laporta, presidente del Barcelona, junto a Sisco Pujol y Xavier O’Callaghan. También Josean Querejeta, presidente del Baskonia, con Félix Fernández. Y José Ángel Sánchez, director general del Madrid, y su adjunto, Carlos Ocaña. Los 36 representantes de los 13 clubes accionistas disfrutaron anoche de una cena de gala donde quedó de manifiesto que están más unidos que nunca. Tienen muy claro que el proyecto de la Euroliga está dando los pasos hacia el futuro por el mejor camino posible.

articles.title: Dylan Ennis niega que el UCAM Murcia juegue "sucio" y Renfroe le recuerda a Sadiel Rojas
articles.standfirst: "Hago una pregunta seria. ¿Realmente cree la gente en España que jugamos sucio? Esta es mi cuarta temporada con el UCAM y nunca he sentido que lo hayamos hecho"
articles.summary: "Hago una pregunta seria. ¿Realmente cree la gente en España que jugamos sucio? Esta es mi cuarta temporada con el UCAM y nunca he sentido que lo hayamos hecho"
articles.body: Dylan Ennis, jugador canadiense del UCAM Murcia, publicó un mensaje en su cuenta de X (Twitter) para desmentir la supuesta leyenda urbana de que su equipo utiliza el "juego sucio" sobre la pista. "Hago una pregunta seria. ¿Realmente cree la gente en España que jugamos sucio? Esta es mi cuarta temporada con el UCAM y nunca he sentido que lo hayamos hecho. Sí, jugamos con intensidad; sí, practicamos una defensa que desgasta a los rivales. Es un estilo diferente, pero ¿sucio? No estoy de acuerdo con eso. ¿Me equivoco?", publicó Ennis en un comentado mensaje. Alex Renfroe, base estadounidense con pasaporte bosnio que jugó en Valladolid, Baskonia, Barcelona, Manresa, Burgos, Granada, Bilbao, Betis y Fuenlabrada, no dudó en contestarle a Ennis y recordarla figura de Sadiel Rojas. "Sí. Todo el mundo lo decía. Gran parte de ello tenía que ver con Sadiel Rojas, ya que él era una pieza clave de la identidad", publicó en X sobre el alero dominicano que jugó en Murcia de 2014 a 2023. En 2020 Sarunas Jasikevicius declaró, cuando era entrenador del F.C. Barcelona, que "sabía que el Murcia iba a jugar supersucio, al límite de la falta". En 2022 Jasikevicus declaró que "teníamos que dar también las hostias que pega el Murcia". En 2022 el Gran Canaria denunció al juez único el "comportamiento violento y antideportivo" de Sadiel Rojas, que tiene su número 12 retirado, por un codazo que le propinó en la cara AJ Slaughter. El UCAM Murcia respondió presentando una denuncia ante la ACB por "incitación al odio" contra Sadiel Rojas. El equipo murciano recopiló publicaciones ofensivas cuyos autores son "actores principales de la ACB".

articles.title: Gilbert Arenas: "Nuestra basura, los tíos que no pueden mantenerse en la NBA, son los mejores de Europa"
articles.standfirst: Gilbert Arenas replica a Nikola Jokic atacando al baloncesto europeo
articles.summary: Gilbert Arenas replica a Nikola Jokic atacando al baloncesto europeo
articles.body: Gilbert Arenas, carismático y controvertido jugador de la NBA de 2001 a 2012 que se suma a la teoría conspirativa que pone en duda los éxitos de Michael Jordan, respondió a la sugerencia de Nikola Jokic de que los jugadores de la NBA deberían jugar en Europa para mejorar su desarrollo. La teoría de la estrella de los Nuggets es que "en Europa y en la selección nacional, lo más importante es ganar el partido. Sé que suena tonto. Pero en esta liga, se ve que algunos jugadores necesitan anotar, conseguir puntos, lo que sea, mejorar sus estadísticas. Pero en la selección nacional y en Europa, lo más importante es ganar, y ojalá todos los jugadores de la NBA fueran a jugar a Europa solo para ver la presión que hay allí". Gilbert Arenas replicó a Jokic ante DeMarcus Cousins recordándole el oro olímpico de Estados Unidos, "así es como os ganamos a vosotros y a Francia. No nos importaban las estadísticas. Ganamos el oro. Si es a eso a lo que te refieres... Os pateamos el culo". "Hemos hecho que esta mierda guste. Somos el estándar del baloncesto", le apuntó Cousins. Posteriormente dirigió sus dardos en su programa contra la Euroliga: "Nosotros no necesitamos disputar la Euroliga. Nuestra basura, los tíos que no pueden mantenerse en las plantillas de la NBA, van allí y son los mejores jugadores de Europa. Son americanos los mejores de todos aquellos países".
